How to Place NFC Review Cards in Your Store for Maximum Scan Rates

Discover the strategic placement techniques that turn passive storefront visitors into active Google reviewers. Learn how physical positioning directly impacts your local business reputation and review volume.

Target High-Dwell Time Areas

The secret to getting more taps on your NFC review cards is placing them where customers naturally pause and wait. High-dwell time locations include checkout counters, waiting room coffee tables, and dining payment folders.

When customers are standing in line or waiting for a receipt, they are often looking at their phones out of boredom. Presenting an NFC card right at eye level during this exact moment removes friction and invites an effortless tap.

Train Your Staff to Make the Ask

Even the best-designed NFC and QR review card needs a human introduction to truly thrive. Equip your front-line staff with a simple, friendly script to mention the feedback process naturally during the interaction.

For example, cashiers can say, 'If you loved your service today, just tap your phone on the little stand before you leave—it really helps our small business!' This verbal cue dramatically increases the likelihood of a customer actually engaging with the technology.

Combine NFC Technology with QR Codes

While NFC is incredibly fast for modern smartphones, not every customer has their NFC settings enabled or understands how the tap feature works. Always ensure your physical cards also feature a clearly printed, high-contrast QR code as a reliable backup.

By offering both options on a single display stand, you accommodate every single customer regardless of their device type or tech-savviness, ensuring zero missed opportunities for a five-star review.

Track and Rotate Your Display Locations

Don't just set up your review cards once and forget about them. Monitor which locations generate the highest volume of scans over a two-week period and adjust your merchandising strategy accordingly.

If the front counter isn't performing as well as the exit door, move the display. Keeping the cards fresh and integrating them into seasonal counter displays also prevents 'banner blindness' among regular, returning customers.
